analysis:
Examined all supplied workflow text, patches and metadata against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. No concrete security regression is established in this scope. These are CI Actions caches, not the encrypted inference-prefix storage governed by T-041; no supplied change alters prompt encryption, tenant scoping, serving authorization, billing or privileged runtime controls.
provider-release-cache.yml:81-93 now exports CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off for darkbloom-named runners without a cache URL. Its master/dispatched warming still uses Blacksmith (lines 52-65), and unsigned handoff validation remains (106-125). provider-tests.yml adds the same choice before cache operations and guards the visible restore/save steps, including fixture and metadata caches. The new cached-.git screening (head 107-132 and repeated blocks through 1232-1257) rejects symlinks, active hooks and selected execution/include configuration before integrity checks and checkout. This improves the prior fsck-only handling; it is not proof that arbitrary cached repositories are safe.
provider-plan.yml:174-185 changes lane sizes and adds independently routed GPU shards; provider-tests.yml:907 consumes those routes. No supplied evidence proves that resource reductions cause security-relevant failures or that routed runners violate artifact trust.
Integration must inspect darkbloom-route.yml and the relevant build/cache consumers: verify runner naming and cache-URL provenance, cache namespace isolation between untrusted PRs and release builds, and that provider-release-build plus setup-python honor CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off. The release-cache workflow itself only sets the flag. Also reconcile revised GPU-test workloads with the formerly documented high memory use. These contracts matter to A-017/T-054 build provenance and CI availability but are outside the supplied implementations; they are questions, not findings. Unchanged caller and dependency behavior has not been audited.
